A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dichotomy between the two types of nebular lines can be explained if the nebulae are not homogeneous and contain a cold, metal-rich component.

the observed dichotomy can be explained by a combination of two effects: (1) a temperature gradient, with the cold H-deficient gas emitting all heavy element ORL fluxes and (2) a metallicity gradient, with the warm H-rich gas emitting all light element ORLs and all CELs.

the dichotomy between CELs and ORLs is not a real one, as it is often assumed in the literature, but rather a manifestation of the fact that the nebulae contain two distinct components of plasma with different physical conditions and compositions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the traditional approach to nebular diagnostics, which assumes that the observed nebular emission is entirely due to the diffuse warm plasma, is fundamentally flawed.

the traditional nebulae diagnostics are incomplete, and that the observed dichotomy is not due to the presence of two physically distinct components, but rather due to the presence, in addition to the hot, ionized plasma, of a cold component that is invisible in the optical and ultraviolet.
